utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Since when have you known him, and how did you come to know him, could you tell us that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: I have known Mr. Vasiljevic personally since he came to Visegrad or, rather, since his father bought the house near my own house, quite near my own house. I know him since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: How long is that, from now going backwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Probably more than 25 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that his father bought the house and that they lived in that house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. His father bought the house, but Mr. Vasiljevic, Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic, lived in the house alone, of course, before he married.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know -- if you know that he married, do you know his family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes, I know his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did he have to build his family house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: No, the house had already been built.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You mean the house he moved into and lived at the time, that's what you're thinking of, but do you know that next to that house, a new house was built?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vasiljevic personally, himself, built himself a house, a new family house. He built it himself later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say "built," that would mean that it was completed and that they had moved into it. Now, do you know how long it took him and whether he actually completed the building of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: The family house belonging to Mr. Vasiljevic I think had a roof before the war. It had a roof over it, but they moved in only after the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know that when the house was completed, that he rented out the house and lived in his old house? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vasiljevic went on living in the old house and he let the new house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember who he let it to? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. Members of SFOR were in -- it was rented out to the SFOR members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I should now like, sir, to go back to the time when the JNA had left Visegrad and when you, yourself, were transferred from doing your job in Visegrad and went to join the security for Bikavac and as you said, yourself, were able to go home from time to time. Now, do you happen to remember whether during that period of time, you saw Mr. Vasiljevic or learnt from somebody else where his whereabouts were, whether he had mobilised and, if so, where to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: When I first went home, and the first couple of times, I didn't see Mr. Vasiljevic, but I heard from his wife that he had been deployed as a cook to some unit. I think the place was Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say, sir, at first when you went home you learnt about this, now, as -- after the 19th of May, you started doing your job at Bikavac. Can we say that what you are talking about now was the period after the 20th of May or, rather, the end of May 1992; would that be the period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes, precisely that period. That means after the 19th and 20th of May to the end of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember whether after talking to his wife and learning that from her, whether you happened to see him personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. When I was on leave another time, I saw Mr. Vasiljevic in front of his family house, and he confirmed himself that he had indeed been sent to be a cook in Prelovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Can you remember or if you can remember, when you talked to him on that occasion, was he wearing a uniform of any kind, and if so, what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: As there were very few people in uniform to begin with in the TO, I think Mr. Vasiljevic at the time was wearing an old uniform of the former JNA type, which is the olive-green type of uniform that the former JNA soldiers used to wear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was that a uniform which at that time, that is to say, before the departure of the JNA, was worn by the reservists who had been issued uniforms of that kind and kept them at home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you remember whether on the occasion he had any weapons on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: As he was at home, I'm sure he didn't have any weapons on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You saw him in front of the house. I think that's what you said. So he was in uniform, but you couldn't notice any weapons on him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. His house is right up by the road, and I saw him passing just in front of his house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And he told you on that occasion that he was in fact in Prelovo and working in the kitchen there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: Yes. I think he also told me that that was his training from the regular army, that when he was in the regular army, he had been a cook, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: When you say regular army, you mean when he was doing his military service in the JNA, I assume. Is that what you meant, or did you mean his reserve formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD22
utterances.text: No. I meant his regular military service in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, I had said that Tuesday evening we would look at how we're going with the list. I don't think that we ever contemplated that your client would be in the box for quite so long, but notwithstanding that, we're keeping up pretty well to the timetable you have provided, and I rather suspect that we will run out of evidence unless you can get some -- at least another witness along. Is it possible for you to get another witness this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, in agreement with the Victims and Witnesses Unit. We're going to have a talk now, and they tell me that there is the possibility of them bringing one or two witnesses in to be here if we finish the witnesses we have before the end of the week, that they would have two ready witnesses. So are we -- may I just ask you, inquire whether we're working on Friday afternoon or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, we certainly are. I think we, having lost the two-week spell there, we've got to keep moving. And you did get that second week on the basis that we were sitting full time. So I don't think I have to take the whole of the blame for it. But certainly I think you should get somebody along if you can, because I suspect that these witnesses will move a little bit more quickly than you've anticipated. Very well. We'll adjourn now and resume at 9.30 tomorrow morning.
